headline: State desk: Massachusetts backs drive-throughs; California delays labels
dek: Massachusetts regulators voted on 17 November to advance drive-through sales, California pushed a Poison Help label rule to July 2027, and Texas bills target patients and jobs.
key_points: Massachusetts' Cannabis Control Commission voted on 17 November 2026 to move ahead with drive-through service at licensed dispensaries.
California will not enforce its new Poison Help number rule for edibles and drinks until 1 July 2027, if retailers hand out a safety brochure meanwhile.
Texas lawmakers pre-filed HB 330 to widen medical access and HB 507 to protect workers who test positive for cannabis.
Sweet Flower workers in Los Angeles authorised a strike ahead of Green Wednesday.
body: The evening state desk picks up four changes from the last day: a vote in Massachusetts, an enforcement delay in California, more pre-filed bills in Texas and a labour fight in Los Angeles. Each touches how cannabis reaches customers, from the car window to the label to the person behind the counter.

The Massachusetts Cannabis Control Commission voted at its 17 November meeting to move forward with allowing drive-through service at licensed dispensaries, The Marijuana Herald reported. That follows our morning report that the item was on the agenda.

Massachusetts allowed curbside pickup during the pandemic, but that permission expired on 31 December 2023. A permanent drive-through option would give stores another sales channel and could help medical patients with disabilities or limited mobility who struggle to enter a shop. The commission had studied a petition on the subject through a working group, and Commissioner Kimberly Roy has stressed that drive-through windows are different from the temporary drive-up service of the pandemic.

The vote is a step, not final rules. It sits inside the broader rewrite under the reform law Governor Maura Healey signed in April, which doubled the adult possession limit to two ounces and raised the retail licence cap per company from three to six. Voters rejected the Question 8 repeal measure earlier this month by roughly three to one.
## California: Poison Help labels can wait

California's Department of Cannabis Control told licensees on 16 November that it will not enforce a new labelling rule for edibles and cannabis beverages until 1 July 2027, according to The Marijuana Herald. Assembly Bill 2532, signed by Governor Gavin Newsom on 30 September after passing 40-0 in the Senate and 74-0 in the Assembly, requires the national Poison Help number, 1-800-222-1222, on labels or package inserts from 1 January 2027.

During the six months from 1 January to 30 June, retailers selling edibles or drinks without the number on the pack must give buyers a consumer education brochure created under Senate Bill 540. That lets brands use up existing packaging.

Other parts of AB 2532 start on 1 July 2027. Multi-serving drinks in clear containers must show serving lines, retailers must offer a free measuring device that holds at least one fluid ounce and measures to a tenth of an ounce, and brands may not market multi-serving drinks as single servings.
> Three of today's four items are about the last metre of the sale: the window, the label and the worker who hands it over.
## Texas: medical access and job protection

As we reported on 10 November, Texas Democrats pre-filed adult-use legalization bills HB 362 and HB 369 in the House, with SB 237 in the Senate, for the session that opens on 12 January 2027. NORML reported on 17 November that two more House bills are now in: HB 330 would widen access under the Texas Compassionate Use Program, and HB 507 would bar employers from penalising workers because they are enrolled in that programme or test positive for cannabis metabolites.

NORML says Texas police made more than 29,000 marijuana-related arrests in 2025, about 14% of the national total, and that 98% were for simple possession. Our view: employment bills often move further than full legalization in divided legislatures, because they do not create a market. The new Democratic leadership in Austin, including Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin, has said THC regulation is a priority.
## Los Angeles: Sweet Flower workers vote to strike

Workers at Sweet Flower dispensaries in Los Angeles, represented by UFCW Local 770, voted to authorise an unfair labour practice strike, Ganjapreneur reported. The union has filed charges with the National Labor Relations Board alleging the company has not bargained in good faith, including cancelled sessions and a late contract proposal. Workers have been under an expired contract since 8 March and were due back at the table on Wednesday. The committee pointed to Green Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving and one of the year's biggest cannabis sales days.

Watch for draft Massachusetts drive-through rules and the public comment window. Watch California brands' packaging changes before 1 July 2027. Watch the Texas Legislature from 12 January 2027. And watch whether Sweet Flower and its workers reach a deal before Green Wednesday on 25 November.
